messages:
mike: Noticed elevated east-west retransmits from GPU inference replicas after the Cilium 1.23.4 rollout in west1 (RDMA-enabled nodepool). Pods stream video frames and we see stall/reconnects intermittently.

rhea: Which AZs and nodepools? Any pattern with RDMA vs non-RDMA nodes?

mike: Affected: west1-a and west1-b GPU nodepools (ib0 present). west1-c (non-rdma) looks fine. TCP retransmits up ~2.4% on p99 windows.

sam: Can you paste the iperf and 'ip link' on an impacted node? Also any kernel dmesg spikes?

mike: paste: 
```
# iperf3 -c pod-ip -P4 -t15
[SUM]   5.2 Gbits/sec  Retr: 1250/52000 (2.4%)
```
```
$ ip link show dev geneve0
6: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1406 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 02:42:ac:11:00:02 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
```

mike: dmesg shows repeated: "skb fragmentation: unexpected GSO state" and "bpf_gso: disabled due to legacy path" during flows.

lee: 1406 MTU is odd; our expected tunnel MTU should be >=1450 to accomodate encapsulation for host MTU 1500. Did 1.23.4 change tunnel floor or add a lower mtu-min?

deploy-bot: Deployment record: cilium/1.23.4 -> k8s-west1 at 2026-02-11T19:08Z by @deploy-bot. Config changed: tunnel.mtu-min=1400, bpf_gso=off (temp).

sam: That config explains it. Disabling bpf_gso on devices with RDMA creates mismatch: ib0 still advertises GSO, tunnel has GSO off -> kernel splits small fragments and RDMA path fails to coalesce.

rhea: Customers are reporting p99 latency spikes on inference endpoints. Need mitigation ASAP. Options: rollback to 1.23.3 on a small canary, rollback across west1, or adjust host MTU to jumbo and lift tunnel floor. Host MTU change requires reboots and cordons.

mike: Kicked off a canary rollback to 1.23.3 on two nodes in west1-a now. I'll monitor counters for 10m.

sam: Also capture 'ethtool -k ib0' and 'sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter' from the affected host; we saw offload toggles in previous incidents.

mike: ethtool -k ib0: gso: on, tso: on, gro: on. Tunnel (geneve0) shows gso: off. rp_filter=0.

lee: With that mismatch, rollback should help. If rollback fixes it we'll pause the rollout and ask Cilium for a patch that preserves GSO on RDMA-aware hosts.

cilium-oncall: We're aware. Upstream pull request proposed to rework bpf_gso detection for RDMA devices (PR #3491). We're testing an eBPF shim that preserves GSO when underlying device supports it.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback started: cilium -> 1.23.3 on west1-a at 2026-02-11T19:27Z.

mike: Canary metrics after 6m: retrans reduced 2.4% -> 0.12%, p99 latency drop 180ms -> 24ms. Streams stabilized. :white_check_mark:

rhea: Pause the 1.23.4 rollout across west1/west region. Create incident and assign infra-networking + cilium-oncall. Escalate GPU customer tickets.

sam: I'll add kernel traces and reproduce steps into the incident with the exact logs. TL;DR: tunnel mtu floor + disabling bpf_gso caused GSO/TSO mismatch across tunnel vs ib0 on RDMA nodes -> skb fragmentation and packet loss on high-throughput east-west flows.

mike: Creating playbook items: 1) rollback document, 2) host MTU jumbo plan (for long-term), 3) test matrix for future cilium releases with RDMA+GSO permutations.

cilium-oncall: We'll prioritize the PR and publish a fixed 1.23.5 build with the shim. Expect candidate tomorrow; we'll coordinate canary testing.

mike: Keeping this thread as primary source. Will update when we approve the patch or schedule host MTU changes.

deploy-bot: Incident opened INC-2026-2103, severity: high, assigned to infra-networking and cilium-oncall.
